evidence.ROLE-DRUNK-001: src/core/engine/setup.test.ts::the Drunk and Lunatic masks never become bluffs or public information (TB-DRUNK-01) — the dealt player keeps roleId 'drunk' while shownRoleId is a Townsfolk mask, and the public view hides both.
evidence.ROLE-DRUNK-002: src/core/engine/engine.test.ts::a Drunk shown the Monk takes the Monk step and protects no one (TB-DRUNK-01) — the Drunk wakes as the Monk, produces no protected effect, and the Imp's attack still kills the chosen player.
evidence.ROLE-DRUNK-006: src/core/engine/tb-audit.test.ts::a Drunk shown the Soldier dies to the Imp (TB-DRUNK-01, TB-SOLDIER-01) — the Drunk who believes they are the Soldier is killed by the Imp's attack.
evidence.ROLE-EMPATH-002: src/core/engine/engine.test.ts::the Empath step is built with the number shape on every night (TB-EMPATH-01) — the step's infoKind is 'number', so the answer is a count and never identifies which neighbour is evil.
evidence.ROLE-FORTUNE-TELLER-002: src/core/engine/engine.test.ts::the Fortune Teller step is built for two players with the yes-or-no shape on every night (TB-FORTUNETELLER-01) — the step's infoKind is 'yes-no', so the answer never identifies which of the two is the Demon.
evidence.ROLE-MONK-003: src/core/engine/engine.test.ts::Monk protection and Soldier safety stop the Imp (TB-MONK-01, TB-SOLDIER-01) — the Monk-protected player remains alive after the Imp attacks them.
evidence.ROLE-SAINT-002: src/core/engine/engine.test.ts::the Saint's night death does not lose the game (TB-SAINT-02) — after the Imp kills the Saint, checkWin returns null.
evidence.ROLE-SAINT-003: src/core/engine/engine.test.ts::Saint loses on execution and Mayor wins at three alive without execution (TB-MAYOR-01, TB-SAINT-01) — the executed Saint's winner is team 'evil' with reason 'saint'.
evidence.ROLE-SCARLET-WOMAN-004: src/core/engine/engine.test.ts::a registered-dead player does not count toward the Scarlet Woman's five (TB-SCARLETWOMAN-01) — with four registered-alive players the Scarlet Woman does not inherit and winner.team is 'good'.
evidence.ROLE-SPY-002: src/core/engine/engine.test.ts::a Spy beside the Demon may register as good to the Chef (TB-CHEF-02, TB-SPY-01) — the host-supplied 'good' Spy registration changes the Chef's count from 1 to 0 while needsChoice is true.
evidence.ROLE-GRANDMOTHER-006: src/core/engine/bmr.test.ts::the Grandmother cannot choose an evil grandchild (BMR-GRANDMOTHER-02) — the first-night step rejects the Demon and an evil-aligned Outsider, then accepts a good player and stores setup.grandmotherId.
evidence.ROLE-LUNATIC-005: src/core/engine/setup.test.ts::the automatic Lunatic mask follows a Demon chosen later and reaches the dealt card (BMR-LUNATIC-01) — the dealt Lunatic keeps roleId 'lunatic' and receives the in-play Demon as shownRoleId.
evidence.ROLE-TINKER-001: src/core/engine/engine.test.ts::a sober Tinker dies from an ability death during the day and the night (BMR-TINKER-01) — tinkerDeath is allowed in the day and the night and records cause 'ability' with bmr 'tinker'.
evidence.ROLE-TINKER-004: src/core/engine/engine.test.ts::a protected Tinker does not die from their ability (BMR-TINKER-01) — a Tea Lady-protected Tinker stays alive with no death record, and the same command kills once the Tea Lady is poisoned.
evidence.ROLE-ZOMBUUL-005: src/core/engine/bmr.test.ts::the Zombuul's second death is real and wins for good (BMR-ZOMBUUL-01) — the second death sets alive false and winner team 'good' with reason 'demon-dead'.

gaps.ROLE-DRUNK-003: The mask test asserts that the public view hides the real and shown roles, but no test asserts the Drunk player's own view or knowledge; the sentence is information-only.
gaps.ROLE-FORTUNE-TELLER-003: The cited herring test asserts only that a configured red herring answers yes; no single test asserts the first-night assignment of a good player or that the herring stays the same all game.
gaps.ROLE-MAYOR-006: Three separate tests cover the dead, Soldier and Monk-protected redirect branches; no single test asserts the sentence's three-target disjunction.
gaps.ROLE-POISONER-004: The only evidence is the Slayer-specific TB-SLAYER-01 test; no test asserts the generic poisoned once-per-game rule.
gaps.ROLE-RECLUSE-002: The registration test asserts good/evil and Minion/Demon options only; it does not assert an Outsider registration or different registrations in one night.
gaps.ROLE-SPY-003: The registration test asserts the good/Townsfolk/Outsider option set even when dead, but no test asserts different Spy registrations during one night.
gaps.ROLE-VIRGIN-002: The cited test asserts the immediate execution and the cleared nomination ledger; it does not assert the transition to night or that a second execution is impossible.
gaps.ROLE-VIRGIN-003: The cited tests assert the nominator stays alive and the Virgin is spent; neither asserts that voting continues.
gaps.ROLE-EXORCIST-005: The cited test covers the Pukka and Shabaloth continuing abilities; no test covers the Zombuul branch of the sentence.
gaps.ROLE-GOON-005: The cited test asserts the alignment change only; no test asserts that the Goon's character is unchanged.
gaps.ROLE-LUNATIC-001: The setup test asserts the real role and the shown Demon mask, but no test asserts the Lunatic's own knowledge of the real character or alignment; the sentence is information-only.
gaps.ROLE-BARON-003: No test asserts the composition after the Baron dies; TB-BARON-01 covers setup composition only.
gaps.ROLE-BARON-004: No test asserts the Drunk setup instructions triggered by the Baron; the cited rows cover the Baron's composition and the Drunk's mask separately.
gaps.ROLE-BUTLER-004: The only cited Butler vote test asserts the opposite engine behavior: an illegal vote is counted with a private host warning, not that the Butler must lower their hand.
gaps.ROLE-BUTLER-006: No test covers a dead Butler's vote; the cited tests cover the night choice, the master record and the illegal-vote warning.
gaps.ROLE-BUTLER-007: Traveller exile is not modelled; no test asserts that exile is not a vote.
gaps.ROLE-CHAMBERMAID-005: BMR-CHAMBERMAID-01 counts only steps that woke; no test covers a drunk or poisoned player still counting as having woken.
gaps.ROLE-CHEF-004: Travellers are not modelled; no test covers evil Travellers counting for the Chef.
gaps.ROLE-COURTIER-002: The cited test chooses the in-play character 'fool'; choosing a character absent from the game is not asserted.
gaps.ROLE-COURTIER-004: No test asserts that the Courtier learns nothing about whether the choice succeeded.
gaps.ROLE-COURTIER-005: No cited test covers an impaired Courtier's choice; the only such test carries no engine rule ID.
gaps.ROLE-COURTIER-006: No test covers the Courtier's own impairment suspending and later restoring the target's drunkenness.
gaps.ROLE-COURTIER-008: The engine and its tests cover one Courtier; no test covers a second copy and only one player becoming drunk.
gaps.ROLE-DRUNK-005: No test asserts that an ability checking character type treats the Drunk as an Outsider; the cited tests cover the mask and public view only.
gaps.ROLE-EMPATH-004: No test asserts the Empath's night order relative to the Demon or that its answer is taken at dawn; TB-EMPATH-01 tests the computed count only.
gaps.ROLE-EXORCIST-006: No test asserts a blocked Demon still waking for another ability; BMR-EXORCIST-01 tests only the blocked own step.
gaps.ROLE-FORTUNE-TELLER-004: No test asserts the red herring's or the Fortune Teller's ignorance of the herring's identity.
gaps.ROLE-FORTUNE-TELLER-005: The cited dead-player test selects only the Fortune Teller's own seat; no cited test chooses a dead Demon and asserts a yes.
gaps.ROLE-FORTUNE-TELLER-006: No cited test covers the host choosing a good red herring, including the Fortune Teller themself; the setup command test is not cited by an engine rule.
gaps.ROLE-FORTUNE-TELLER-007: Storyteller advice for small games; no engine behavior or test.
gaps.ROLE-GAMBLER-004: No test asserts the absence of feedback; the cited test asserts only death on a wrong guess and survival on a correct one.
gaps.ROLE-GAMBLER-006: The pinned Gambler r3073 Summary contains no impairment sentence; the claim restates the generic drunk/poisoned rule and no Gambler test carries an engine rule ID for it.
gaps.ROLE-GODFATHER-004: BMR-GODFATHER-02 tests a day execution and a day with no death; no test covers an Outsider killed at night.
gaps.ROLE-GODFATHER-005: No test covers two Outsiders dying in one day and the Godfather still making only one kill.
gaps.ROLE-GODFATHER-006: No test covers an Outsider executed but saved, and the Godfather not waking that night.
gaps.ROLE-GOSSIP-002: No test asserts that the statement must be definite, audible and understood; the engine records only the host's truth answer.
gaps.ROLE-GOSSIP-005: No test covers a true statement made while impaired followed by recovery before the night kill.
gaps.ROLE-GOSSIP-006: No test covers the Gossip dying before the scheduled night death.
gaps.ROLE-GOSSIP-007: Storyteller advice about choosing a target that will die; no engine behavior or test.
gaps.ROLE-GRANDMOTHER-001: The cited tests assert the stored grandchild and the Demon-kill trigger; no test asserts the Grandmother is shown the grandchild's character.
gaps.ROLE-GRANDMOTHER-002: BMR-GRANDMOTHER-02 tests the good/team target only; no test asserts that the Grandchild does not learn about the Grandmother.

gaps.ROLE-INNKEEPER-005: No test covers the Innkeeper choosing themself, becoming drunk and thereby losing the protection.

gaps.ROLE-LUNATIC-006: No test asserts the Lunatic's real team (Outsider, good); BMR-LUNATIC-01 tests the mask and bluffs.

gaps.ROLE-MONK-006: No test asserts the dawn announcement wording.
